findings.title: Async goroutines use request context that will be cancelled after response is sent
findings.body: All async goroutines (Create line 51, Delete line 110, Update line 135, DeleteCollection line 163) derive their timeout context from the parent request context via `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`. Once the HTTP handler returns and the response is sent, the request context is cancelled, which will immediately cancel the child context. This means the asynchronous legacy writes will almost certainly fail with a context cancellation error, defeating the purpose of the dual-write safety net. The goroutines should use `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` (Go 1.21+) or `context.Background()` with any necessary values copied over.

findings.title: Create records legacy duration metric on storage error instead of storage duration
findings.body: On line 45, when `d.Storage.Create` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`. Since this is measuring the duration of the storage operation that just failed, it should call `d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...)` instead. This will produce incorrect metrics, attributing storage failures to the legacy store.

findings.title: Update records legacy duration metric on storage error instead of storage duration
findings.body: On line 129, when `d.Storage.Update` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`. This should be `d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...)` since it is measuring the failed storage operation. This produces incorrect metrics.

findings.title: DeleteCollection async goroutine records storage duration instead of legacy duration
findings.body: On line 166, inside the async goroutine that performs the legacy delete-collection, the code calls `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)`. Since this is measuring the legacy operation, it should call `d.recordLegacyDuration(...)` instead. This will produce incorrect metrics, attributing legacy store latency to the storage store.

findings.title: Delete success metric passes `name` as kind parameter instead of `options.Kind`
findings.body: On line 106, `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes the object `name` (e.g. "foo") where the `kind` parameter is expected (e.g. "Playlist"). All other calls in this file pass `options.Kind` in this position. This will produce metrics with incorrect kind labels, making them useless for aggregation by resource kind.

findings.title: Delete sets context logger to d.Log instead of the enriched log variable
findings.body: On line 97, `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` uses the base logger `d.Log` instead of the locally enriched `log` variable (defined on line 96 with name, kind, and method values). This means any logging within the Storage.Delete call or the async goroutine will lack the structured context fields that all other methods include, making debugging harder.

findings.title: Tests cannot verify async legacy writes succeed or fail appropriately
findings.body: The unit tests for Mode3 (Create, Delete, Update, DeleteCollection) set up mock expectations for legacy store calls but have no mechanism to wait for or assert that the asynchronous goroutines actually execute. Since the legacy writes happen in goroutines, the tests may pass even if the goroutines never run or fail immediately due to context cancellation. Consider using synchronization (e.g., channels or WaitGroup) in tests, or at minimum adding a test that verifies the legacy mock was called after a short delay.
